definition: Generating 3D assets by optimizing a 3D representation so its renders satisfy a 2D diffusion prior (SDS), or increasingly by feed-forward 3D generators trained on 3D data.
details: Generating 3D assets by optimizing a 3D representation so its renders satisfy a 2D diffusion prior (SDS), or increasingly by feed-forward 3D generators trained on 3D data. The bridge between image-generation priors and usable game and design assets.

explainer.lead: Text-to-3D generates 3D assets either by optimizing a 3D representation so its renders satisfy a 2D diffusion prior (SDS) or, increasingly, with feed-forward 3D generators trained on 3D data. It matters as the bridge between image-generation priors and usable game and design assets.

tiers.eli5: It is like sculpting an object by looking at it from many angles and adjusting until each view looks right.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers either optimize a 3D representation against a 2D diffusion prior via SDS or use feed-forward generators trained on 3D data. The pitfall of the SDS route is that it relies on a 2D prior, so consistency across views is not guaranteed.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, one route optimizes a 3D representation so its renders satisfy a 2D diffusion prior (score distillation sampling); the other trains feed-forward 3D generators on 3D data. The known limit of the prior-based route is that a 2D objective does not directly enforce 3D consistency.

explainer.example: Describing a chair in text, then optimizing its 3D representation until renders from multiple angles match the prompt-driven image prior.
